name: Bani
title: Levite and Covenant Renewer
summary: Bani was a Levite who played an important role in the period after Israel's return from the Babylonian exile. He is known for his participation in public reading of Scripture, prayer, and worship during the reforms of Ezra and Nehemiah, and was among those who sealed a covenant with God to follow His law.

keyEvents.title: Public Worship and Praise
keyEvents.description: Bani was among the Levites who led the people in praise and worship when Ezra read from the Book of the Law to the assembled congregation.

keyEvents.title: Prayer and Confession of Sin
keyEvents.description: Bani took part in the great prayer and confession of sin where the Levites cried out to the Lord with a loud voice and confessed the sins of the people.

keyEvents.title: Sealing of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Bani was among those who sealed the new covenant, in which the people promised to keep God's law and commandments after returning from exile.

keyEvents.title: Teaching the People the Law
keyEvents.description: Bani was among the Levites who helped the people understand the Law while Ezra read it aloud at the Water Gate.

keyEvents.title: Descendants Among Those Who Sent Away Foreign Wives
keyEvents.description: Among Bani's descendants were some who had taken foreign wives and were required to send them away during Ezra's reform.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in David's Genealogy
keyEvents.description: A Bani from Gad's clan is mentioned as one of David's mighty men, and the name also appears in several genealogies, highlighting its significance in Israel's history.
